title: keyboard manager steals completely CTRL after few hours of running

judgment.rationale: Several users report that Ctrl ceases to reach ordinary applications while Keyboard Manager remaps may still work. One current 0.100.2 RDP user supplied a concrete full-screen/windowed transition sequence, and a later user confirmed the failure on Aug 27. The trigger is intermittent, so the state transition and root cause remain unconfirmed.
evidence: The thread has 15 comments with reports across Windows 10/11 and multiple PowerToys releases.
A July 23 reporter described RDP full-screen, windowed, and full-screen transitions on 0.100.2, after which Ctrl shortcuts become plain letters; KM-defined Ctrl+H still works.
A separate June 18 reporter said left Ctrl is detected but ordinary Ctrl shortcuts, including on-screen keyboard input, fail while Ctrl remaps continue.
The last comment on Aug 27 says exiting PowerToys immediately resolved a fresh occurrence.
judgment.recommended_action: Have a maintainer replay the documented RDP transition on a current build and trace modifier key-up/state cleanup at the failure boundary.

fix_assessment.rationale: Stale modifier bookkeeping after a focus/session transition is plausible, and recent modifier cleanup fixes show relevant code paths, but the reports do not prove a shared root cause. A bounded tracing and regression-test design is warranted.

proposed_fixes.title: Reconcile Ctrl hook state across RDP and focus transitions without disrupting active remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A Ctrl key-up or focus/session transition may not be reconciled between the low-level hook's physical state and Keyboard Manager's logical state, leaving ordinary applications without Ctrl even while the remap engine continues to consume the modifier. This remains a hypothesis.
plan: Reproduce the reporter's RDP full-screen to windowed to full-screen sequence while capturing physical Ctrl down/up, foreground-window, and session/focus transitions.
Trace the modifier state reset and cleanup paths in KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp to identify the first point where ordinary Ctrl and the remap engine diverge.
Add an event-sequence regression test for the observed missing/reordered key-up or focus transition before changing state handling.

If a stale logical state is confirmed, reconcile only the modifier state invalidated by that transition, preserving intentionally active remaps and avoiding synthetic key-up events for physically held keys.
verification: After repeated RDP full-screen/windowed transitions, ordinary Ctrl+A/C/V works on both local and remote desktops.
Keyboard Manager Ctrl remaps continue to work and do not leave Ctrl stuck.
The test covers the exact observed event ordering and adjacent held-key/release orderings.

confidence.rationale: The intermittent symptom and one detailed RDP sequence are well evidenced, but no event trace identifies the lost transition and the thread contains more than one trigger pattern.

issue_context.summary: Ctrl periodically stops reaching ordinary application shortcuts while Keyboard Manager-defined mappings may continue to function; toggling/restarting Keyboard Manager or changing RDP focus temporarily restores normal behavior.
known_information: The RDP reporter confirmed the issue on PowerToys 0.100.2 and supplied Windows 11 24H2 remote and 25H2 local environments using Microsoft Japanese IME.
Their steps are remote desktop full-screen, repeated typing/Ctrl shortcuts, exit to windowed mode, type locally, return to full-screen, then observe Ctrl+key being processed as the key alone.
The issue has multiple independent reports, including a fresh Aug 27 occurrence.
Related stuck-modifier and AltGr cleanup changes exist in source history, but none is confirmed to resolve this exact sequence.
inferences: A missed or stale modifier state across RDP/focus transitions is plausible but not proven.
The reports may include distinct trigger paths that converge on the same visible symptom.
issue_context.analysis: The RDP reporter already supplied a useful reproduction sequence and explicitly said the failure is not reliably reproducible, so another generic step request or log request is unnecessary. Focused maintainer replay and event-state tracing can narrow the hypothesis without claiming a confirmed cause.
initial_investigation: Read the full live issue and all 15 comments, including the 0.100.2 RDP sequence and the newest Aug 27 report.
Checked current labels, assignees, linked duplicates, and referenced reports.
Inspected KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp modifier cleanup paths and focused recent history; related changes do not establish that the current report is fixed.

actions.label: Trace and reconcile Ctrl state across RDP focus changes

design.title: Reconcile Ctrl hook state across RDP and focus transitions without disrupting active remaps

reproduce.title: Reproduce Ctrl shortcut loss through RDP full-screen transitions
prerequisites: Current upstream main or a current build
Local Windows 11 and remote Windows 11 sessions connected with mstsc.exe
Keyboard Manager enabled; optional Ctrl remap to confirm mapped shortcuts remain functional
steps: Connect to the remote PC using mstsc.exe in full-screen mode.
Type on the remote PC and use Ctrl+key shortcuts.
Exit RDP full-screen to multi-window mode and type/use Ctrl+key shortcuts locally.
Return to RDP full-screen and continue typing and using Ctrl+key shortcuts.
If ordinary Ctrl shortcuts degrade, test Ctrl+A/C/V and a Keyboard Manager Ctrl mapping before toggling or restarting the module; capture the hook/focus event sequence.
reproduce.expected_result: Ordinary Ctrl shortcuts and configured Ctrl mappings remain functional on local and remote sessions after repeated focus/full-screen transitions.
